what: EdgeGuard connected to the public ETSI MEC Sandbox (try-mec.etsi.org) from the team laptop (Samsung Galaxy Book2 Pro, 8 GB RAM, Windows 11, Docker Desktop)

sandbox.network: Sandbox network scenario (stationary / low-velocity / high-velocity UEs), mep1
sandbox.location_api: location/v3 (the dashboard lists v2; v2 paths answer 404, v3 answers 200)
sandbox.rnis_api: rni/v2 (queries/rab_info answers 200; no layer2_meas cell load in this scenario)

path: ETSI MEC Location API -> MEC-IPE (tools/mec_ipe.py) -> Mobius IN-CSE resources -> subscription -> EdgeGuard MEC app
notes: Connection verified: live Sandbox UE positions reach the MEC app only through oneM2M resources written by MEC-IPE.

No alerts is expected: the Sandbox UEs are city-scale (hundreds of metres apart) and no worker/forklift pair came within assessment range; collision-risk behaviour is evaluated with our own warehouse scenario (scenarios/edgeguard-warehouse.yaml).
RNIS cells were discovered (10 containers) but the scenario publishes no cell load, so the congestion margin stays off.
